lesson.grammar_point: saying and hearing numbers, prices and totals

listenings.text: Good afternoon, and here are the offers of the day. Children's T-shirts are twelve pounds, or two for eighteen. Shoes are fifteen ninety-nine this week, and that is down from thirty pounds, so it is half price. Scarves and hats are fourteen eighty-one, and if you buy three you pay only forty. In the food part, the coffee is four fifty and the bread is one seventy. And a small note about paying: the machine for the card is working again today, so you can pay by card or in cash, as you prefer. If you pay in cash, please check your change before you leave the till. Thank you, and have a very good afternoon.

Hello, this is a message for Patricia from the store on Oxford Street. I am calling about Tuesday. There was a mistake at the till and we charged you twice for the shoes, so we owe you fifteen ninety-nine. I am very sorry about that. There are two ways to solve it: you can come to the store and we give you the money in cash, or we can put it back on your card, and that takes three working days. If you prefer the card, you do not need to come, just call us and say yes. If you come, please bring the receipt from Tuesday, the one with the total of forty-two eighty. We are open from nine to seven, every day except Sunday. Thank you, and sorry again.

extra_audio.text: How much is it in total, please? Sorry, how much? Can you say the number again? Can you write it down, please? Thank you very much.
